description: Open-source SenseVoiceSmall model for Mandarin, Cantonese, English, Japanese, and Korean ASR, language ID, emotion recognition, and audio event detection.

summary.one_liner: SenseVoice is a multilingual speech foundation model (the SenseVoiceSmall checkpoint) for speech recognition, language ID, speech emotion recognition, and audio event detection, with Python, ONNX, Libtorch, and llama.cpp/GGUF inference paths.
keywords: detect laughter or applause in audio
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides the SenseVoiceSmall speech model and reference code for ASR and language identification across Mandarin, Cantonese, English, Japanese, and Korean, plus emotion tags and audio event tags (such as bgm, applause, laughter, crying, coughing, sneezing). Python usage goes through FunASR with an FSMN-VAD model to segment long audio, and optional punctuation and inverse text normalization. It includes a bounded-memory long-audio script that runs fixed 30-second overlapping windows without VAD, and a composed speaker-diarization example using CAM++ speaker labels. Inference can also be run via ONNX (funasr-onnx) or Libtorch (funasr-torch), and a llama.cpp/GGUF path provides a standalone binary without Python. The repo also includes a FastAPI service, Docker build files, a WebUI script, and finetuning data-prep and training instructions.
use_cases: transcribe Chinese, Cantonese, English, Japanese or Korean audio
tag laughter, applause or other sounds in audio
run offline speech-to-text on CPU without Python
serve speech recognition over an HTTP API
fine-tune a speech model on domain-specific data
notable: Single self-contained llama.cpp/GGUF binary with built-in FSMN-VAD and no Python at runtime
Rich transcription output that includes language, emotion, and audio event tags
Non-autoregressive architecture, claimed over 5x faster than Whisper-Small at similar parameter count
Long-audio script with bounded overlapping windows and raw per-chunk outputs preserved
Clarified license terms for official SenseVoiceSmall weights in the README
caveats: Released SenseVoiceSmall checkpoint covers only five languages; the 50+ language figure refers to broader research work
Speaker diarization is a composed pipeline with separate CAM++ and VAD models, not an output of the checkpoint; the README says it was not validated for diarization accuracy
Fixed-window long-audio mode can change recognition at cut boundaries; the Docker GHCR image is private, so local build is needed
Model weights follow a separate FunASR Model Open Source License, not the MIT license of the code
